lead: the words took under a minute and there were about forty of them, said in front of a room, and everything else you have kept since arrived one sentence at a time and was never said out loud.
sun: nobody asked you to ring her father. you have done it every other sunday for years, off a sentence in a car and the half-beat before she said fine, and it went into the undertaking that week without a word spoken about it. the ear keeps producing obligations in exactly that form — arriving whole, needing no discussion, and answerable only by somebody who heard them.
moon: and The Crown takes nothing back off. what went in at year two is in at year thirty, whether or not the thing it answered still exists — her father has been dead since spring and the sunday is still yours, given to the sister now. the undertaking only grows. nothing here releases a line, including the lines nobody set.
pull: you said about forty words that afternoon. what you have kept since is a much longer document, written one overheard half-second at a time, and she has never seen a line of it.
tension: the marriage gets called an easy one, and by every visible measure it is: no bad year, no separation, nothing anybody outside had to be told. the difficulty has no wording. you are keeping an agreement she did not enter and cannot read, and the honest account of it says you have been hearing her for thirty years and acting on what came back. that sentence ends easy marriages.
cost: a bond here comes through the things that end other bonds, because strain gets answered in the week it starts and never becomes a subject. she keeps her end exactly — the forty words, entire, for thirty years, and that is not a small thing to keep. the two of you are honouring agreements of different size, both in good faith, and only one of you knows the sizes.

lead: you go in first because of a year printed in a book, and by the time the room settles you already have the true position of everybody in it, and nobody in it has yours.
sun: precedence puts you at the end of the speaking order, so every account in the room has reached you before your turn. you get the item and you get what is under it — who conceded before arriving, which objection is being held back for later, whose agreement is only in the voice. the sentence you finally say is short, lands, and reads as judgement matured over decades.
moon: above you is where all of this used to go — a senior, someone older, a person whose job includes being told. The Heart closed that early, by a date, which cannot be appealed and will not move. the intake did not slow to match. it goes on filling at the same rate into a position with nothing over it.
pull: everything a room is carrying arrives at you and stops there. the last person you could have handed any of it to went off the register before most of them were admitted.
tension: somebody nineteen years in disagrees with you and takes it to a corridor instead, because the only address for a complaint about you is you. so it comes back round by the long route, weeks late, with the heat out of it. the deference is genuine and aimed at the year, and none of it touches the reason the place has held, which is that you hear an arrangement giving way and go at it in the same week.
cost: nobody in that body has left badly, because a person deciding to go is audible about a year before they say so, and you get to them first. what you learn doing that has no next stop. it sits with you, at the top of an order that runs one way, and the two people who could once have taken any of it off you are dead.

lead: at fifteen you heard where the story had been mended — an old man's voice going careful on one word, at a table where it gets told every year — and you have been under it ever since.
sun: it arrived as sound. a half-second of care in a voice, at the year the account passes over, taken in the way everything is taken in here — without a request, without an argument, without any option of not receiving it. it has gone on arriving. every retelling since has carried its own small adjustment, made by people who believe every word, and no two of the adjustments sit in the same place.
moon: The Root took it from there and has not been talked out of a level since. under the story is a decision; under the decision is the year it was made in; under that is what the people making it were short of. seventeen years of records, and no point where the going gets easier to justify and none where it stops.
pull: the bottom of where you come from is not a scandal. it is somebody in a bad year picking the version people could live inside, and you have heard yourself do the same thing.
tension: the people who gave you the story are not liars and you have known that from the start, which removes the one version anybody would find easy to hear. it comes out again at gatherings, warmly, to children, and you say nothing, and the saying nothing gets read as a coolness about where you come from. what you object to is a sentence somebody needed in a year that nearly finished them, and no toast has room for that.
cost: you can get under an account that a whole community depends on and come out with the actual cause, and be right, which almost nobody manages about their own people. the going down does not end. and the year your own children ask, you will hear the care go into your voice at the same word, in the same place, and you will say it anyway.

lead: in any week the true condition of about twenty people arrives at you, unasked and complete. you will act on a fifth of it. the choosing takes a second and nobody appointed you to make it.
sun: the intake has no filter. the one whose marriage is going, the one whose money is going, the one who is only bored — all of it at the same volume, none addressed to you, most from people who would say nothing was wrong if asked. and each item arrives with the thing that would answer it already attached. you are not handed problems. you are handed problems with the week's work in them.
moon: the deciding is positional, from your seat at the outer ring, where the shape is plain and the sort costs nothing. this one holds till summer, that one goes this week, that one settles itself. The Flock is fast and mostly right. what it ranks is other people's lives against each other, on a judgement nobody submitted to, and a thing set down at that speed stays down.
pull: nothing gets to choose whether it reaches you, and you choose what happens to all of it. the ones you set down are not told, and they are still telling you.
tension: the phrase is that you always know what matters, and it names the part that costs nothing. picking the one thing in a week that will actually come apart takes a moment from where you sit. the rest — the ten people whose real state also came in and got set down — has no name, and putting it into words would produce a register of everyone you decided against.
cost: in that circle, the thing that would have gone badly gets picked out of an ordinary week and answered while it is still nothing. the sorting does not lighten it. the ones you put down come back in the winter with the same thing, warmly, because you are still the only place any of it goes, and the week refills at the rate it always did.
